newsitem.title: UK: Granada motorway sale gets top price.
newsitem.headline: Granada motorway sale gets top price.

text.p: British hotels and leisure group Granada Group Plc said on Tuesday it had agreed to sell its motorway service station network to Bahrain-based Investcorp for 476 million pounds ($765.3 million) -- beating market expectations.
Granada sold 21 Welcome Break service stations in Britain to Investcorp, one of a short list of four bidders, which included ASDA Group Plc and venture capital group CinVen.
Investment analysts said the deal, plus the sale of the two London and New York Westbury Hotels for 90 million pounds that was announced at the same time, was very good news for Granada.

"The market was expecting a good price and I think we've got one that was significantly ahead of expectations," said Greg Feehely at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson. Feehely said the price for the hotel sale was slightly disappointing, but the overall package was good news.

Granada acquired the Welcome Break business when it won control of hotel and catering empire Forte just over a year ago after a gruelling takeover battle. Competition authorities ordered Granada to sell Welcome Break by April to meet monopoly concerns.
Granada said the deal represented a multiple of 22 times historic earnings and a premium to net book value of 142.6 million pounds.

The firm said it had decided not to sell the Grosvenor House hotel on London's exclusive Park Lane. Analysts said this might have hit the shares, which fell immediately after the announcement, but then bounced back to close 0.5 pence higher at 930.
The Grosvenor House accounted for some 300 million pounds of a total book value of 800 million for 17 luxury hotels which Granada had planned to sell.
"Granada believes that the best value for shareholders will be achieved by retaining and improving the hotel rather than by a disposal at the current time," the company said.
The Westbury deal means it has now disposed of five of the properties.

The firm has netted more than 1.2 billion pounds from disposals since its 3.9 billion takeover of Forte. The money will go towards reducing debt which was around 3.5 billion pounds after the Forte deal.
Investcorp plans to invest 50 million pounds in the Welcome Break business over the next few years and is looking at expanding it in Britain, and possibly also into continental Europe.
Richard Warner, a member of Investcorp's management board said the group wanted to develop the Welcome Break brand, but in the long term might consider floating the business.
"We have long term plans to realise our investment in the company," he said in an interview, adding that could be achieved by a flotation or other means.
Michael Guthrie, who ran the Pavilion motorway services chain until he sold it to Granada, will become chairman of Welcome Break, Warner said. ($ = 0.621 British Pounds)
